err_backend_unreachable: Error: Could not reach the backend.
console_empty: No commands have been run yet.
reboot_confirm: Are you sure you want to reboot the device?
shutdown_confirm: Are you sure you want to shut down the device? You will need physical access to turn it back on.
system_desc: Run system diagnostics. Output appears in the panel below.
network_desc: View network status and manage configuration.
ctrl_net_diag_desc: View detailed interface and port information.
ctrl_ipconfig_desc: Assign a static IP or revert to DHCP. Changes are written to /etc/dhcpcd.conf and take effect after a reboot.
net_err_static_required: IP address and gateway are required for static mode.
ctrl_hostname_desc: Rename this device on the network. Only letters, numbers, and hyphens are allowed.
hostname_prefilled: Current hostname pre-filled — click Rename to apply.
hostname_read_fail: Could not read current hostname — try refreshing.
hostname_success: Hostname updated successfully. Reboot to apply fully.
ctrl_smb_desc: Control the Samba file sharing service (smbd).
tunnels_desc: Manage remote access tunnels. Enabling a tunnel exposes this device beyond the local network.
ctrl_tailscale_desc: Join or leave the Tailscale network. Allows secure remote access via a private VPN mesh.
ts_authkey_placeholder: Auth key — optional, for headless setup (tskey-auth-...)
ts_timeout: Tailscale up timed out — check if auth is needed.
ctrl_ngrok_desc: Expose local ports to the internet via ngrok tunnelling. Auth token must be configured on the device first.
ngrok_not_found: URL not found — click Check Status for log
ctrl_newt_desc: Open-source alternative to ngrok. Connects this device to your Pangolin server over a secure WireGuard tunnel. Create a Site in Pangolin to get a Newt ID and secret.
newt_secret_saved_placeholder: Saved — leave blank to keep it
newt_hint_auth_failed: Pangolin rejected the Newt ID or secret. Check them against your Site in Pangolin.
newt_hint_error: Newt can't reach the Pangolin server. Check the endpoint address and this device's internet connection.
newt_hint_docker_unavailable: Newt needs Docker, and the backend can't use it.
newt_connected_msg: Tunnel is up. This device is reachable through Pangolin.
newt_still_connecting: Still connecting. Click View Logs to see what Newt is doing.
newt_fix_intro: Pick one of these, run the commands in a terminal on this device, then click Check Again.
newt_docker_ok: Docker is working now. Click Enable to start Newt.
newt_err_endpoint: Enter the Pangolin endpoint, e.g. https://pangolin.example.com
newt_err_id: The Newt ID should be letters and numbers only.
newt_err_secret_chars: The secret should be letters and numbers only.
newt_starting: Starting Newt... the first time can take a minute while it downloads.
newt_conflict_confirm:
Another copy of Newt is already running on this device:

{list}

If it uses the same Pangolin Site, the two will keep disconnecting each other, and anything reached through that tunnel (such as a web SSH session) may drop.

Start Newt anyway?
newt_conflict_cancelled: Not started. Another copy of Newt is running on this device.
newt_docker_access: {error} See below for how to fix it.
newt_started_waiting: Newt started. Waiting for the tunnel to connect...
newt_stopped_msg: Newt stopped. Your settings are saved for next time.
newt_no_logs: No logs yet. Newt isn't running. Fill in the details above and click Enable.
newt_setup_first_updates: Set up Newt above first. Updates are checked once it is running.
newt_update_err_tunnel: {error} If you opened this page through the tunnel, reload it in a minute.
newt_check_waiting: Downloading the latest Newt image to compare. This can take a minute.
newt_update_confirm:
Update Newt now?

Newt restarts, so the tunnel drops for a few seconds. If the new version doesn't reconnect within a minute, the previous version is put back automatically.
newt_update_waiting: Updating Newt and waiting for the tunnel to reconnect (up to a minute)...
newt_rollback_confirm:
Go back to the previous version of Newt?

The tunnel drops for a few seconds while Newt restarts.
newt_rollback_waiting: Restarting Newt on the previous version...
newt_auto_setup_first: Set up Newt above first, then turn on automatic updates.
docker_desc: Monitor and control Docker containers running on this device.
docker_overview_desc: View running containers, available images, and live resource usage.
docker_manage_desc: Enter a container name then choose an action. Logs shows the last 100 lines.
docker_remove_confirm: Remove container "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
docker_run_desc: Pull an image and start a new container. All fields are validated before the command runs.
docker_run_output_start:
Running: docker run {image}...
This may take a while if the image needs to be pulled.
docker_timeout_output:
Request timed out — the image may still be pulling in the background.
Use List All to check if it started.
llama_desc: Run a language model on this device. Off by default so it uses no memory.
ctrl_llama_enable_desc: Starts the llama service. The rest of the panel keeps working either way.
ctrl_llama_recommended_desc: Tested on the Xerxes Pi and known to run well. Download one with a single click.
llama_recommended_load_fail: Could not load the list of recommended models.
ctrl_llama_model_desc: Paste the download link of a .gguf file from Hugging Face, then download it to this device.
llama_installed_empty: No models installed yet. Download one above.
llama_switch_off_to_change: Turn Llama off to switch models.
llama_need_model: Download a model first, then try again.
llama_loading: Loading {model}. Small models are ready in a few seconds; larger ones can take a minute.
llama_stopped_early: Llama stopped right after starting. The model may be too large for this device's memory, or llama-server hasn't been built yet (run make llama).
llama_stopped: Llama stopped. Its memory has been freed.
llama_err_no_url: Paste a Hugging Face download link first.
llama_err_bad_url: Use the link to a .gguf file, like https://huggingface.co/<user>/<repo>/resolve/main/<file>.gguf
llama_downloading_msg: Downloading {file}. Large models can take several minutes — keep this tab open to see the result.
llama_still_downloading: Still downloading after an hour. The device keeps going in the background — check Installed models later.
llama_delete_in_use: Turn Llama off to delete the model it's using.
llama_delete_confirm: Delete {model} from this device? You'll need to download it again to use it.
chat_greeting: Hello! I'm your Xerxes Pi assistant. How can I help you manage your server today?
chat_err_timeout: No reply after 3 minutes. The model may be too large for this device. Try a shorter question or a smaller model.
chat_err_backend: Could not reach the backend. Check the panel is still online.
chat_err_llama_off: Llama is turned off. Turn it on in the Llama tab, then send your message again.
chat_err_loading: The model is still loading. Try again in a few seconds.
i2c_desc: Manage devices connected over the I2C bus.
oled_power_desc: Shows the chosen information on the OLED screen. When off, the screen is blank. Stays as set after a restart.
oled_state_idle_hint: Not in use: the display is only driven while it is on.
oled_content_desc: Choose what the screen shows. The preview updates as you make changes. Press Save to send them to the display.
oled_mode_qr: QR code to this admin panel
oled_content_saved: Saved. The display will update in a few seconds.
oled_content_saved_offline: Saved. The display will show this once it is reconnected.
oled_settings_desc: Which I2C bus and address the OLED is on. The defaults suit the 128x64 SSD1306 on the Xerxes Pi's Qwiic port. Some panels use 0x3D instead.
oled_err_no_bus: I2C bus {device} was not found. Check that I2C is enabled (raspi-config → Interface Options → I2C).
oled_err_no_device: The display did not respond at {address} on {device}. Power off the Pi, then check the Qwiic cable and the address.
oled_err_write_failed: Lost contact with the display. Your settings are kept and will be shown again once it reconnects.
oled_err_unsupported: This build cannot drive the display (it needs Linux with I2C). The preview still works.
oled_err_probe_timeout: The display did not respond in time.
oled_err_invalid_stat: One of the chosen items is not supported.
oled_err_no_stats: Choose at least one item to show.
oled_err_invalid_bus: I2C bus must be a number from 0 to 1023.
oled_err_invalid_address: I2C address must be from 0x03 to 0x77.
oled_err_save_failed: Could not save the settings. The change applies until the backend restarts.
rfid_reader_desc: When on, tapping a registered tag runs its command on this device with the backend's privileges (root when deployed). Unknown tags are logged and ignored. Stays on after a restart.
rfid_mod_idle_title: Not in use: the reader is only polled while it is on, scanning or live scanning.
rfid_on: Reader on. Tap a registered tag to run its command.
rfid_off: Reader off. Tags will not run commands.
rfid_log_placeholder: Tag reads and command output appear here while the reader is on.
rfid_log_tagfile_error: Tag file error, no commands run: {error}
rfid_log_finished: Command finished with exit code {code} ({secs} s)
rfid_tags_empty: No tags registered. Add one below.
rfid_tags_file_error: Error: {error} The file has not been changed; fix or remove it to manage tags here.
rfid_add_desc: Scan a tag on the reader (or type its ID), then enter the command to run when it is tapped.
rfid_scan_place: Place an RFID tag near the Xerxes Pi...
rfid_scan_place_secs: Place an RFID tag near the Xerxes Pi... ({secs} s)
rfid_scan_module_err: Can't reach the RFID module: {error} (retrying, {secs} s left)
rfid_scanned: Scanned: {id}. Enter the command to run, then click Add Tag.
rfid_scanned_type: Scanned: {id} ({type}). Enter the command to run, then click Add Tag.
rfid_scan_timeout: No tag detected. Hold the tag flat against the reader and try again.
rfid_already_registered: Tag {id} is already registered with command: "{command}"
rfid_err_need_id: Scan a tag or enter its ID first.
rfid_live_desc: Shows every tag held to the reader, whether it is registered, and the raw read details. Live scan itself never runs commands; the reader still does if it is on.
rfid_live_empty: Start a live scan, then place tags near the reader.
rfid_live_empty_running: Live scan running: place tags near the reader.
rfid_live_empty_failing: No tags can be read until the RFID module is connected.
rfid_settings_desc: Which I2C bus and address the RFID module is on, and where tags are stored. The defaults suit the PiicoDev module on a Xerxes Pi. I2C must be enabled (raspi-config → Interface Options → I2C).
rfid_err_bus: I2C bus must be a number, e.g. 1 for /dev/i2c-1.
rfid_defaults_filled: Defaults filled in. Click Save to apply.
